notes:
PASS on the fake backend: python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/robots/zzy5510__ur5-grasp-and-kinect-demo-on-gazebo --backend fake exited 0. Evidence state is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. Model-authored by deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017, run ros-wave-c-106; driver.lock.json keeps reviewed_by null. No human reviewed or tested this package, no hardware was attached, and no ROS graph, Gazebo, MoveIt or live simulator was run.

SHAPE AND CARD HINTS. The card's family and helper are used unchanged: a configuration-only ROS 1 RosDriver with no Python native class. The card's hints and device_plan name Robotiq85Gripper and GripperIO from the separate robotiq_85_driver (a Python Modbus hardware class under src/UR_with_Robotiq_grasp_gazebo/ur_tc/robotiq_85_gripper/robotiq_85_driver). That node is not started by the shipped simulation launch: main.launch:7-12 starts launch_simulation.launch and MoveIt, and launch_simulation.launch:43-48 loads arm_controller_ur10.yaml and gripper_gazebo_trajectory.yaml and spawns arm_controller and hand_controller. The readme.md says the robotiq_85_gripper package was abandoned. The integrated device is therefore the Gazebo simulation environment that the card's role (sim-env) describes, not the unused hardware gripper driver. The card's candidate classes were not adopted literally; the four used extensions are listed in catalogue_requests. No entry_symbols were required for a RosDriver.

SCOPE. Declared endpoints: private /gazebo/pause_physics and /gazebo/unpause_physics (std_srvs/Empty), /clock (rosgraph_msgs/Clock), /joint_states (sensor_msgs/JointState). The pause/resume services are created by GazeboRosApiPlugin on the node named gazebo with the private ~ handle (gazebo_ros_api_plugin.cpp:122,140,430-445); the callbacks call world_->SetPaused(true/false) (1626-1636). /clock is advertised at line 221 and publishSimTime is a world-update hook (line 201, 2091-2110). /joint_states is advertised by JointStateController through the root node handle (joint_state_controller.cpp:57) using the shipped controller configuration (joint_state_controller.yaml:1-3). NOT COVERED: the arm FollowJointTrajectory controllers and MoveIt planning/execution, the hand_controller gripper path, the Kinect image and point-cloud streams (camera/rgb/image_raw, camera/depth/image_raw, camera/depth/points and camera_info), the robotiq_85_driver topics, and all other Gazebo services (spawn, model state, reset, set physics properties). The package is not a controller and does not command joint motion.

SAFETY. The simulated device is R2 because it contains a UR5 arm; the independent stop is the input-free safe_state=True pause action, also bound as the e-stop service. The service acknowledgement proves only that the Gazebo callback returned; it is not sensed quiescence. The shipped demo drives the arm through MoveIt and FollowJointTrajectory controllers, which this package does not cancel; a pending controller goal can continue after an unpause. mhs.safety.reset clears only the software latch and leaves the world paused (no reset binding, SAFE-042); only the explicit resume action unpauses it, and that action is refused while latched. This is a simulator stop, not a physical emergency stop.

FAKE. fake.py subclasses RecordingRosTransport and models only the declared services and subscriptions. It is an analytic contract fake, not a recording: no ODE physics, gazebo_ros_control, MoveIt, planning, contacts, camera or wall-clock loop. All clock and joint values are placeholders, and the fake answers neither subscription while paused, matching the silent world-update and controller-update paths. The fake returns eight joint entries (six arm joints plus two gripper joints) as placeholder test data; a live /joint_states may publish a different set and additional joints. The fidelity block records F0, no determinism, timestep_ms 0, realtime_factor 0, reset none and snapshot_restore false.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked both Gazebo service bindings (relative pause_physics and unpause_physics on the private handle of the node named gazebo, gazebo_ros_api_plugin.cpp:122, 140, 430-445, in the vendored gazebo_ros_pkgs), the two observations, all 18 facts and the stop against the plugin, the shipped launch files, the xacro/URDF chain, the controller configurations and the vendored drivers at the pin. The stop holds as a simulator pause: pausePhysics sets the world paused before answering (1626-1630), repeated calls are idempotent, there is no reset binding (the latch reset leaves the world paused), and the observations are explicit subscriptions, so nothing waits on the topics that go silent while paused. Defects: the joint-state output declared rad, rad/s and N.m for every entry although the spawned model2.urdf (through ur_with_kinect.xacro) makes arm_to_finger1 and arm_to_finger2 prismatic (366-396); the arm-joint fact cited arm_controller_ur5.yaml while the launch loads arm_controller_ur10.yaml; two facts said more than their lines (a 'not while paused' inference on line 201, the Kinect plugin and camera prefix outside kinect.xacro:50-54); and nothing said that the Gazebo GUI the launch opens by default or the vendored spawn_robot_tools move_model can unpause, that the clone vendors ur_modern_driver with ur_bringup and robotiq_85_driver for real hardware, or that the arm model uses UR10 meshes and offsets. The reviewer changed the three joint arrays to unit 1 with per-joint units, re-cited the arm-joint fact to the loaded ur10 configuration, narrowed and widened those two facts, added eight source facts, rewrote safe_state and the docstring and added three gaps (driver.py), updated facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate and collect.py --strict pass with the expected G1.CLONE_NOTE and G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE warnings and the digest unchanged (sha256:9e8fc001f8962e20b79dc19f4838c1138d1bfbc840903ff7453db6633582fa30); the author's joint units in rad for all entries are superseded. The card needs the owner's publication decision (publish_review required; licence not stated (NOASSERTION)); the package may not be published or merged into a published tree before it. For the human reviewer: Simulated UR arm with a two-finger gripper (ROS 1, Gazebo, MoveIt). The e-stop pauses Gazebo physics through the vendored gazebo_ros plugin; an active FollowJointTrajectory goal is held, not cancelled, and continues as soon as anything unpauses the world (the resume command, the Gazebo GUI play button, which the shipped launch opens by default, or the vendored spawn_robot_tools move_model); /clock and /joint_states are silent while paused. The package binds no motion command. The clone also vendors ur_modern_driver with ur_bringup for a real UR arm and robotiq_85_driver for a real Robotiq gripper (serial /dev/ttyUSB0); on such a graph /gazebo/pause_physics does not exist and the MHS e-stop fails with the latch held, so any hardware use needs a human review and an independent physical stop. Licence NOASSERTION, publish_review required.
